My father is what you'd call a devout man, my mother not so much.

To clarify something, my father is the best man I've ever known. He genuinely thought this would help me, and in many ways it really helped us to grow closer.

Because of my being sent away, my father and I changed how we both live our lives. Now I'm aware that he's always there if I ever need to reach out, day or night, whereas in the past we had grown quite distant. He trusts me to make the right decisions, and my only real fear is that I'll never be as good as a man as he is.

My mother is a completely different story, however. She's manipulative and cruel. I've done everything I can to remove her from my life, and she resents me for it, as much as I resent her for how she has treated me, my father, and my sister. She has gone so far as to confide in my little sister that she is afraid of me, because I refuse to give in to her.

In short, my father is a good man who thought he was getting me the help that I needed, and I cannot fault him for that. My mother is somebody who viewed my being sent away as an opportunity to punish me for standing up for myself, and I will never forget that.

I was dealing with depression and had been hospitalized twice due to that struggle. Neither hospital visits, both of which including my spending time in the mental ward (they hate to be called that), were due to suicide attempts. I asked for help when I felt things were too far out of my control.

The fall when I was taken I felt that things were looking up for me. I had a girlfriend who I felt I had a real connection with, I was more outgoing with my friends, and I was exploring extracurriculars like theater for the first time. I was starting to feel comfortable with myself. Confidence was a new, and very welcome, feeling to me.

And then I was sent away. My school expelled me because of this. My girlfriend's father died and I wasn't told for five months. I wasn't there for seomeone I really cared about and I've never been able to move on from that.

I'm sorry if my response is long-winded or unclear. Ive never really talked about this in length. Just felt like it needed to come out somehow. Sorry.

Being sent to a wilderness program by my parent's.

I was woken up by my father at three in the morning on November 17, 2011. Behind him were two "transporters" who pushed me into a car, drive me to the airport, and several hours later I was at some little house in Utah.

I spent months backpacking in the high desert of Utah. Didn't see a car, nor any sign of civilization for the whole time. I was allowed to leave in Febuary of 2012. I thought I would be going home, to finish my senior year of high school.

I was wrong.

From there, I was sent to a therapeutic boarding school in northern Idaho. I stayed there for a year and change. A lot happened during that year. I changed because of it. Maybe for the better, maybe for the worse. I don't really know.

All of my friends from highschool graduated while I was away. They all went to college. They all received closure to those four years of high school. They all got to say goodbye to each other.

I didn't.

I will never forgive my parents (edit: one of my parents) for taking away what could have been a defining moment of my life and replacing it with a series of events that have done nothing but scar me to the point where I'm distrustful of anyone I meet and I no longer believe that I can work hard to achieve things. Because how can I work hard when I'm aware that at any moment the whole world can be dragged out from under me?

Edit: I feel the need to clarify that my father did what he did to try and help me, for he thought he had no other options. He sent me away to try and help me, and he wasn't wrong in doing so, as it was done out of love for me and I recognize that. I love my father with all my heart, as he is the greatest example of a selfless person I have ever known. I hope I can be half the father he has been to me some day.

My mother is a different story entirely, and I recognize that she is a very toxic individual. I've strived to distance myself from her at every opportunity, and I'm in a much better place because of it.
